content.introduction: The Federal Reserve, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, left its key interest rate unchanged at around 3.6% after two days of deliberations, marking the fifth consecutive meeting with no change in the benchmark rate. Warsh held a news conference to reiterate the Fed's commitment to combating inflation, acknowledging the challenges and stating, "We have no magic wand. This isn’t something we’re going to be able to carry out in days or weeks." Warsh also welcomed the vigorous debate at the committee meeting, describing it as a "good family fight."
body:
READ MORE: How much longer will consumers be willing to muscle through higher prices?

After the Fed announces its rate decision, Warsh will speak at a news conference, where his remarks will be closely watched for hints about the Fed's next steps. He will likely repeat the Fed's desire for a "timelier" return of inflation to the 2% target. Some may view that as a sign the Fed will boost its key rate at its next meeting, in December, a move already widely expected by Wall Street investors. [...] WASHINGTON (AP) — The Federal Reserve is expected to stand pat on interest rates Wednesday even though inflation has accelerated in the past couple of months as the Iran war has caused spikes in oil and gas prices.

Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh is expected to hold a news conference at 2:30 p.m. EDT. Watch live in our video player above. [...] The Fed, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, wants to return inflation to its 2% target, which it typically does by raising its short-term interest rate. Higher borrowing costs, over time, can cool spending and slow inflation. The Fed raised its key rate last month for the first time in three years, from about 3.6% to 3.9%, in what many investors and economists perceived was a first step toward a renewed effort to bring down inflation.

WASHINGTON (AP) — The Federal Reserve left its key interest rate unchanged Wednesday, although three officials dissented in favor of higher rates as the central bank wrestles with how to deal with persistently high inflation.

Watch Fed chair Kevin Warsh's news conference in our video player above.

The Fed's rate-setting committee reached its decision after two days of deliberations, marking the fifth straight meeting at which the benchmark rate was kept at around 3.6%. [...] READ MORE: Inflation cools more than expected in June as gas costs fall and underlying prices ease

At a press conference following the rate decision, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the Fed's commitment to combatting inflation. At the same time, Warsh said, "We have no magic wand. This isn't something we're going to be able to carry out in days or weeks." [...] Warsh said he welcomed vigorous debate at the committee meeting. "I asked for a good family fight and I got one,'' he told reporters at a press conference.
